faqs.question: How do I convert RMVB to MP4?

faqs.question: Can I play an RMVB without converting it?
faqs.answer: Yes, in a player that reads RealMedia. RealPlayer HD lists RMVB playback, and ffplay plays supported RealMedia streams. An MP4 plays on nearly every device, which is the usual reason to convert.

faqs.question: Which codecs end up in the MP4?
faqs.answer: Video is encoded as H.264 and sound as AAC. The settings are fixed: x264's ultrafast preset at CRF 32, and 96 kbps for the audio.

faqs.question: Will the MP4 look better than my RMVB?
faqs.answer: No. The MP4 is encoded from the decoded RMVB, so converting adds no detail. It makes the movie playable in more places, not sharper.

faqs.question: Is my movie resized?
faqs.answer: Only when it is big. A movie whose picture exceeds 1920 pixels on the longer side is scaled down to fit that bound, while smaller ones keep their dimensions. faqs.question: Is my RMVB uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. FFmpeg, built as WebAssembly, runs in your browser tab, so the file never leaves your device. The RMVB itself stays as it was; the MP4 is a new copy named after it.

faqs.question: What does an FFmpeg error mean for my RMVB?

faqs.question: Can I convert several RMVB files at once?

faqs.question: Can I just rename the .rmvb file to .mp4?
faqs.answer: No. Renaming changes only the name, and the data inside stays RealMedia with RealVideo pictures. Converting writes an MP4 with H.264 video.

faqs.question: Is there a size limit for the RMVB?
faqs.answer: The page sets no file-size or time limit. A long file takes as long as your device needs.

guide.title: About RMVB files
guide.markdown:
### What is an RMVB file?

RMVB stands for RealMedia Variable Bitrate. It belongs to the RealMedia family from RealNetworks, and the Library of Congress describes the .rmvb ending as variable-bitrate RealMedia video. RealVideo can be encoded toward an average bitrate or toward a constant visual quality, and the versions differ in efficiency: RealVideo 9 and 10 do not code the picture equally well. A RealMedia file can also carry descriptive information such as a title, an author and a copyright line. Its media type is application/vnd.rn-realmedia.

The format was popular for sharing movies in the early 2000s, so RMVB files turn up in old download collections and archived TV episodes. It is a proprietary RealNetworks format, and today it counts as a legacy one, with the older downloaded movies and media archives as its main remaining use. One thing that looks like an RMVB but is not one is the .ram file. It is a small reference file used in some RealMedia streaming setups, and it points to the video instead of holding it.

### Programs that open RMVB files

**Windows**

- RealPlayer HD: the vendor lists playback of RMVB videos, along with its Windows requirements.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FFmpeg: includes a RealMedia demuxer and codec-specific handling.
- ffplay: plays supported RealMedia streams through the FFmpeg libraries.

### RMVB and MP4 compared

- **Names and media types**: .rmvb is application/vnd.rn-realmedia. .mp4 is defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14.
- **Contents**: an RMVB carries RealVideo pictures. MP4 is a wrapper that can hold video made with several codecs, with H.264 and AAC the usual pairing. MP4 turns up in web video, streaming sites and files passed between people.
- **Bitrate**: an RMVB varies its bitrate through the movie. An MP4 holds whatever its encoder produced, constant or variable.
- **Extras**: MP4 can carry metadata alongside the streams.
- **Playback**: nearly every phone, TV and browser plays MP4. Playing one takes a reader for RealMedia and a RealVideo decoder.

The conversion itself: your browser runs FFmpeg, which reads the RealMedia file. Pictures larger than 1920 pixels are scaled down until they fit, anything above 30 frames per second is thinned out, with the running time unchanged, and widths and heights are trimmed to even values. Nothing leaves your device while this runs, and the RMVB itself is never altered. Each finished movie downloads as a new file with your RMVB's name and an .mp4 ending. Then x264 encodes H.264 video with its ultrafast preset at CRF 32, and FFmpeg's AAC encoder writes the sound at 96 kbps. Because the picture is compressed a second time, detail the RMVB had already lost stays lost.

### Other ways to convert RMVB to MP4

- **FFmpeg:** on the command line, `ffmpeg -i archive.rmvb -c:v libx264 -c:a aac archive.mp4` does the job by demuxing the RealMedia file and decoding its RealVideo. Here -i is the input file, and the two -c options pick the encoders for picture and sound. FFmpeg also has a special codec value, copy, that skips re-encoding, but copy would carry the RealVideo pictures over unchanged instead of making H.264, so name encoders as above.
- **VLC:** select Media > Convert/Save, click Add, choose the RMVB and click Open. VLC then shows a Convert window. Type a name for the destination file, pick a profile whose output is MP4 and click Start.

### Problems with RMVB files

- **It won't play on a phone or TV**: an RMVB needs a RealMedia reader and a RealVideo decoder, and many players lack them. Convert the file to MP4 here, or play it in RealPlayer HD.
- **The file is a .ram**: it only points to a stream. Find the actual .rmvb it names.
- **FFmpeg rejects the header**: FFmpeg turns down an invalid RealMedia header instead of guessing. If ffplay cannot open the file either, download it again.
- **A renamed file still fails**: changing .rmvb to .mp4 leaves the RealMedia data inside. Convert the file instead.
- **The download stopped early**: a cut-short or damaged RMVB usually still converts, and the MP4 is then shorter than the movie. Download the whole file again to get the full length.
- **The two halves of a movie are separate files**: converting never joins files. Join the MP4 files in a video editor.

faqs.question: Can I turn several SVG files into one multipage TIFF?

faqs.question: Can I get my paths back from the TIFF?

guide.title: About SVG files
guide.markdown:
### What is an SVG file?

SVG is short for Scalable Vector Graphics. It is an XML-based vector image format and a W3C standard, with SVG 1.0 a Recommendation in 2001 and SVG 1.1 following in 2003. A logo, chart or icon is stored as shapes, paths and text instead of a grid of pixels, which is why an SVG can be enlarged to any size without going soft. Because the format is plain XML text, you can open the file in a text editor and read its shapes, and a text file can also be searched, indexed and compressed. The drawing can be styled with CSS, and the file can include animation and scripting. SVG also supports clipping paths, masks and filter effects. Browsers open an SVG directly, and a web page can embed one too. A gzip-compressed SVG uses the .svgz extension, and the registered media type is image/svg+xml.

Not every SVG is purely vector. Photos can be placed inside one, and they stay at their own resolution however far you zoom. A drawing can also refer to resources outside the file. A font installed on the device shows up, but a linked image or web font never loads when the SVG is drawn as a picture.

### Programs that open SVG files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Inkscape: edits SVG natively.
- Mozilla Firefox: opens SVG files in the browser.

**Web and mobile**

- Google Chrome displays SVG.
- Safari displays SVG on mobile.

### SVG and TIFF compared

- **Content**: SVG holds shapes, text and styling you can edit. TIFF holds pixels in a tag-based structure, and one file can store several images.
- **Size**: an SVG has no fixed pixel size and scales cleanly. A TIFF is fixed at the pixel dimensions it was saved with, so enlarging it later cannot bring the sharpness back.
- **Compression and color**: TIFF allows several compression schemes, deep color and CMYK separations. SVG is XML text. The extensions .tif and .tiff both name TIFF, with the media type image/tiff, and it was developed by Aldus and Microsoft as a tag-based raster wrapper that can hold different color representations.
- **History**: TIFF began in 1986 at Aldus, and its 6.0 revision dates from 1992. Adobe now controls the specification. Classic TIFF stores file offsets in 32 bits, so a file tops out near 4 GB. SVG is a W3C recommendation.
- **Typical use**: TIFF turns up in scanning, archiving, photography and print work, and document imaging, while SVG is the logo, icon and diagram format of web pages.

The steps are short. Your browser renders the SVG and reports its width and height, and those numbers become the TIFF's pixel dimensions. The page adds no scaling, no size cap and no viewBox logic of its own, and it paints no background, so clear areas remain clear. ImageMagick, running as WebAssembly, then saves the pixels as an uncompressed TIFF whose channels are 8-bit red, green, blue and alpha. Because only raw pixels travel, EXIF data, color profiles and XMP packets stay behind. If you need more pixels, enlarge the width and height attributes in the SVG first. Your original SVG is not changed.

### Other ways to convert SVG to TIFF

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick -density 300 logo.svg logo-print.tiff`. The -density option sets the resolution ImageMagick renders an SVG at, and the default is 72 dots per inch. ImageMagick renders SVG through Inkscape, RSVG or its own internal renderer, so the result depends on the installation.
- **GIMP:** GIMP opens an SVG as an image in the usual way. Choose File > Export As to store it in a format other than XCF, and pick TIFF. The TIFF dialog offers compression such as None, LZW, Pack Bits and Deflate. GIMP opens the SVG as a picture of pixels, so keep the original SVG.

### Problems with SVG files

- **Letters are in the wrong typeface**: text is drawn with the fonts your device has, so a stand-in typeface can alter how the drawing looks. Convert the text to outlines in Inkscape before you start.
- **An image is absent**: a picture the SVG only links to is not fetched. Embed it in the file as data.
- **An embedded photo looks blurry when enlarged**: the pixel parts of an SVG keep their original resolution.

guide.title: About SWF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an SWF file?

SWF is the file format of Flash, the web animation and games technology that began at Macromedia and passed to Adobe when it bought Macromedia in 2005. The letters are commonly read as Shockwave Flash, and a source also gives the name Small Web Format. One file can combine vector graphics, timeline animation, bitmap video, sound and ActionScript code. Its registered media types include application/vnd.adobe.flash.movie.

Adobe ended support for Flash Player on 31 December 2020, so SWF files now live in archives of old games, cartoons and banner ads, and it is no longer simple to see them play. An SWF may also refer to outside media instead of containing everything, so an old file can be missing parts it once loaded.

### Programs that open SWF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Ruffle: a Flash emulator, where compatibility depends on the ActionScript features a file uses.

**Windows and Linux**

- Lightspark: an incomplete Flash implementation.

**Mac**

- Adobe Audition: its SWF import pulls out the audio of video files, and it is not an interactive Flash runtime.

**Web**

- Web player from the Ruffle project: runs Flash in a page through WebAssembly, with some APIs still missing.

### SWF and GIF compared

- **Names and media types**: .swf is application/vnd.adobe.flash.movie. .gif is the Graphics Interchange Format that CompuServe introduced in 1987.
- **Content**: an SWF holds vector graphics, animation, video, sound and code. A GIF holds raster frames and nothing else.
- **Color**: a GIF frame draws from a palette of at most 256 colors. A SWF's vector fills and video are not limited that way.
- **Transparency**: GIF has 1-bit transparency, where a pixel is either clear or solid.
- **Sound and interactivity**: GIF has neither.
- **Compression**: GIF compresses each frame with lossless LZW.

What happens here: FFmpeg opens the SWF and builds a palette from its video frames, sampled at 15 fps and scaled to fit 480 pixels with even sides. A second pass then draws every frame with that palette and writes a GIF that repeats forever, so you do not need to choose a loop count. Only the video stream is used, so the sound is dropped and no ActionScript runs. A SWF that ran faster than 15 fps loses its in-between frames. The SWF you chose is never altered.

### Other ways to convert SWF to GIF

- **JPEXS Free Flash Decompiler:** run `ffdec -format frame:gif -export frame frames-out banner.swf`, using the executable for your platform. The wiki documents the -format option, where frame:gif is one of the frame formats. This writes each frame of the SWF as a separate GIF image in the output folder. For frame export the wiki lists PNG, APNG, GIF, AVI and SVG, with PNG as the default.
- **FFmpeg:** for a SWF with embedded video, run `ffmpeg -i clip.swf flash-preview.gif`. FFmpeg's SWF reader handles bitmap, video and audio data, and it skips vector shape tags, so it is not a Flash renderer. The reader covers FLV1, screen video, JPEG and lossless bitmap pictures, with PCM, ADPCM, MP3 and Nellymoser sound.
- **Ruffle plus OBS Studio and FFmpeg:** open the SWF in Ruffle. In OBS add a window or display capture source, click Start Recording and perform the sequence. Check the recording settings under Settings > Output first. Then encode the saved recording as a GIF with FFmpeg. This captures one playing session, including any errors.

### Problems with SWF files

- **Nothing will open it**: Flash Player was retired at the end of 2020. Use Ruffle or Lightspark instead. Lightspark is an incomplete Flash implementation, so it may not cover everything a file uses.
- **A game or animation looks wrong in Ruffle**: Ruffle has not implemented every Flash API, so graphics or behavior can differ from the original. Its compatibility page says most ActionScript 1 and 2 content will work, with some graphical inaccuracies, and that most ActionScript 3 games run well enough to be played.
- **Parts are missing**: a SWF can depend on external files that no longer exist online. Get the whole set of files.
- **FFmpeg reports an error**: the SWF probably holds no video stream, only sound or vector drawing. Try JPEXS for frames or record it with Ruffle.
- **The buttons don't work**: a GIF has no code, so ActionScript controls cannot carry over.

guide.title: About TIFF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TIFF file?

The name TIFF stands for Tagged Image File Format, a raster wrapper first built by Aldus with Microsoft. The 6.0 revision appeared in 1992, and today the specification is under Adobe's control. Because a TIFF can use several compression methods and color representations, it serves scanners, print shops and photo archives, as well as document imaging and high-bit-depth preservation masters.

One TIFF file may hold a run of images, such as the pages of a scanned document. ImageMagick's format list describes extensive strip, tile, byte-order and compression tag controls for it. The endings .tif and .tiff both refer to the format, labeled image/tiff.

### Programs that open TIFF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- GIMP: opens image files for editing, and each export format keeps a different part of a project's properties.
- ImageMagick: reads TIFF and writes it, with compression, strip, tile and byte-order options.

**Mac**

- Preview: lists TIFF in the format menu under File > Export.

### TIFF and SVG compared

- **What they hold**: TIFF stores pixels. SVG describes shapes, paths and text, and can also embed a pixel image.
- **Scaling**: a TIFF is fixed at its pixel size. An SVG made of paths scales cleanly, but an SVG that only wraps a picture does not.
- **Pages**: one TIFF can carry many images. The SVG produced here carries one picture, held as pixels inside an image element.
- **Color**: TIFF supports high bit depth and CMYK. SVG is XML text styled with CSS, so you can open it in a text editor, and every major browser displays it.
- **Typical use**: TIFF belongs to scanning, print and archiving. SVG is the usual choice for site logos, icons, diagrams and maps.

Here is what happens to your file. ImageMagick, compiled to WebAssembly, reads the TIFF in your browser. SVG is not a format it writes, so it produces a PNG of the picture, and the converter then places that PNG inside an SVG as one image element at the same pixel size, with a matching viewBox. The PNG data is stored in the file as base64 text. This is not tracing: no outlines are found and no text is recognized. A multipage TIFF contributes one image only, and the rest of its pages are left out. Pictures beyond roughly 537 megapixels do not convert, and the page tells you the file is too big. The result fits a tool or web page that accepts only SVG files, and your original TIFF is left unchanged. Several TIFFs chosen at once go through one after another, and each SVG is saved under the TIFF's name. For paths you can edit, trace the picture instead.

### Other ways to convert TIFF to SVG

- **GIMP plus Inkscape:** in GIMP, choose File > Export As (Shift+Ctrl+E) to store the TIFF in a format other than XCF, and use PNG. The GIMP manual points to its Files section for details on each format. In Inkscape, import the PNG with File > Import, select it with the Selector tool and open Path > Trace Bitmap. Adjust the options, update the preview and apply the trace. The vector result sits exactly above your picture, so the original stays underneath until you move or delete it.
- **ImageMagick plus Potrace:** run `magick scan.tiff scan.bmp`, then `potrace -s scan.bmp -o scan-outline.svg`. Potrace reads PBM, PGM, PPM and BMP, converts other pixel values to black and white with a threshold, and -s selects the SVG output. Unless you give a resolution with -r, it assumes the input is 72 dpi, and -o names the file the output goes to. Multiple input files are only allowed for multi-page output backends, so trace one bitmap at a time. It does not list TIFF as input, and it traces black and white shapes, so this suits a clean symbol or line drawing better than a photograph.

### Problems with TIFF files

- **A viewer shows only the first page**: a TIFF may hold several images, so use software that shows the full sequence.
- **A program rejects the file**: not every reader understands each private tag, color-profile extensions among them.
- **The file is enormous**: the original TIFF layout counts offsets in 32 bits, so files top out near 4 GB, and BigTIFF widens those fields.

guide.title: About TTF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TTF file?

A TTF file holds a TrueType font. Apple developed TrueType and licensed the technology to Microsoft, and System 7 shipped with it in May 1991. A TrueType font describes scalable character outlines, so letters stay smooth at any size. Its data is arranged in individually tagged tables, which can hold glyph mappings, outlines, metrics and naming information. The registered media type is font/ttf.

The naming table is how a program learns a font's name, and it is where a specimen takes its heading from. A font file with a broken table or a bad offset can fail to display at all.

### Programs that open TTF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FontForge: opens TrueType outlines for editing, including the tables.

**Windows**

- Windows Font Previewer: double-click the font to inspect it before installing.

**Mac**

- Font Book: installs and validates font files.

**Linux**

- GNOME Fonts: previews installed typefaces and installs downloaded .ttf files.

### TTF and PNG compared

- **What they store**: a TTF stores outlines, character mappings and metrics. A PNG stores a grid of pixels, losslessly compressed, with optional transparency.
- **Scaling**: a font scales to any size. A PNG stays at the pixel size it was drawn.
- **Text**: a font can set any words you type. A PNG shows only what was drawn into it, and it cannot be installed.
- **Use**: a TTF goes into an operating system or an app. A PNG goes into a web page, a slide, a document or a review thread, so people can see a typeface without installing it.

Here is how the specimen is made. ImageMagick, compiled to WebAssembly, loads the font in your browser and draws with FreeType. The top line is the font's name, taken from its name table (the full name, or the family name if there is no full name), cut to 64 characters, and a font with no usable name is labeled "TTF font". Below it come the capital letters, the small letters, and the digits with a few punctuation marks. Five more lines repeat one familiar test sentence, each at its own size of 16, 24, 32, 48 and 64 pixels. Everything is black on white inside a 40 pixel margin. The image is only as wide as the longest line needs, between 400 and 2400 pixels. You cannot change the text. It is a specimen, not the font's outlines and not a character map. The download is named after your file with a .png ending, and the TTF itself is not changed.

### Other ways to convert TTF to PNG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick display-face.ttf display-face-preview.png`. ImageMagick's TTF reader gives a preview image of the font.
- **Pillow (Python):** load the font with `ImageFont.truetype`, which loads a TrueType or OpenType font file at the pixel size you give. If the file is not at the given path, Pillow may search the standard font directories for your operating system, and it raises an OSError when the file cannot be read. Create a canvas with `Image.new`, draw your sample with `ImageDraw.text` and that font, then call `save` with a .png name. This takes a short script, but you choose the phrase, colors and size.
- **GIMP:** with the font available in the font selector, create an image, choose the Text tool, pick the font and size, type your sample and export with File > Export As, choosing PNG. The PNG holds pixels, not an editable text layer.

### Problems with TTF files

- **A font that never shows up**: a damaged font can fail to display. Font Book on a Mac can validate a font file.
- **Two copies conflict**: installing two copies of a font can create conflicts, and Font Book can resolve duplicates.
- **It is missing in an app**: a font missing from a third-party application may require that application's own troubleshooting.
- **The converter says it isn't a font**: FreeType could not read the file. Check that it opens in a font previewer.
- **The converter says it has no letters to draw**: the font has no glyphs for the sample lines, as can happen with an icon or symbol font. Draw your own sample with Pillow or GIMP.
- **You need the glyph outlines**: a PNG cannot give them. Open the TTF in FontForge.

guide.title: About TXT files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

Nothing but characters are held in a TXT file. There are no typographic commands in it, and it dictates no page layout, typeface or placement of pictures, so any editor on any operating system can read it. Its MIME label is text/plain, and the charset parameter tells a receiver how the bytes map to characters.

A styled document turns into plain text when it is saved as TXT, since TextEdit strips the styles and formatting when it converts rich text. What the characters look like is decided by whoever opens the file, not by the file.

### Programs that open TXT files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Visual Studio Code: a code editor that opens text files and lets you edit them.
- Vim: a text editor with Windows builds and documented Unix and macOS use.

**Mac**

- TextEdit: the Mac editor that works with plain text documents.

### TXT and JPG compared

- **What they store**: a TXT stores characters and line breaks. A JPG stores a grid of pixels, compressed with some loss, with an adjustable quality setting and no alpha transparency.
- **Look**: a TXT has no typeface of its own. A JPG fixes one, because the letters are already drawn into the picture.
- **Editing**: text in a TXT can be searched, copied and edited. Text in a JPG cannot be selected.
- **Support**: a TXT opens in any text editor, and a JPG is supported everywhere, so the picture is the safer choice when a destination takes only images.
- **Origin**: the Joint Photographic Experts Group defined JPG (ISO/IEC 10918-1) for photographs. The endings .jpg and .jpeg mean the same format.

Here is what the page does with your file. It decodes the bytes, drops terminal color codes and control characters, and turns each tab into spaces at stops every four characters. The text is then drawn on a canvas in your browser as dark text on white in DejaVu Sans. Lines that run long are folded at word breaks, and a single word wider than the page is cut. The picture is drawn at twice its size whenever it stays within 4,096 pixels a side, and the finished canvas is saved as a JPG at 0.85 quality. A text longer than one picture holds is cut, the last line of the picture says where, and the page shows the same notice. Your original TXT is not changed.

### Other ways to convert TXT to JPG

- **GIMP:** create an image and choose the Text tool. Turn on the editor window ("Use editor window") and load the TXT file with the folder icon in the text editor. Pick the font and size, drag a frame so the text fits, then use File > Export As and choose JPEG. GIMP puts the text on a new layer, and the size control offers several units. Check that no text runs off the canvas.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick -background white -fill black -pointsize 24 -size 800x caption:@notes.txt notes-card.jpg`. The caption: operator word-wraps long lines to the width you give with -size, and -font picks a typeface. The -pointsize option really controls the spacing between lines, newlines in the file act as paragraph separators, and -size is required so the wrapping has a width. A security policy can block reading text from a file.
- **Pillow (Python):** read the TXT with the right encoding, create a canvas with `Image.new` (its default color is black, so pass white), draw the lines with `ImageDraw.multiline_text` and a font, and call `save` with a .jpg name. Text containing newlines passed to `ImageDraw.text` is handed to `multiline_text`, and drawing changes the image in place. You decide the size, wrapping and page breaks.

### Problems with TXT files

- **Accented letters look odd**: a file read with the wrong encoding shows valid characters as the wrong ones. Re-save it as UTF-8.
- **Formatting disappeared**: a styled document saved as TXT loses its styling.
- **A table or image is missing**: plain text cannot preserve an image or table as a word processor would.
- **The text is very long**: a picture ends at 4,096 pixels, so a long log or manuscript is cut. Split the text into smaller files.
- **The converter reports an empty file**: a file with nothing but spaces and control characters leaves nothing to draw. Open it in an editor and check that the text is really there.

guide.title: About WAV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

Sound stored in a WAV file sits inside a RIFF wrapper, so WAV names a container, not a single way of encoding audio. The August 1991 multimedia specification from Microsoft and IBM described it. Most WAV files contain linear PCM, the plain sampled form, but other encodings can ride in the same wrapper, which means two .wav files can differ a great deal inside. You will see audio/wav and audio/x-wav used as media types.

PCM is uncompressed, which makes WAV files big but exact. Broadcast WAVE is the variant that holds metadata used in production and in preservation, and the Library of Congress names WAVE among the formats it recommends for audio collections. Keeping a WAV master and making an AAC for listening is a common split. The usual filename ending is .wav.

### Programs that open WAV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Audacity: opens most WAV recordings, including PCM variants.
- ffplay: the player bundled with FFmpeg, which includes a WAV demuxer and plays WAV files from the command line.

**Mobile**

- Firefox for Android: plays WAV, which Mozilla lists among its supported Android audio types.
- VLC for Android: a free media player for Android phones and tablets, whose decoding follows from the media inside the container.
- mpv for Android: an Android port linked by the mpv project.

### WAV and AAC compared

- **Encoding**: WAV is a wrapper that usually holds uncompressed linear PCM. AAC is a perceptual, lossy codec, standardized as MPEG-2 Part 7 and MPEG-4 Part 3.
- **Packaging**: AAC can be carried in MP4, QuickTime or other wrappers. A freestanding .aac file normally uses ADTS framing and is labeled audio/aac.
- **Profiles**: AAC comes as LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2.
- **Quality**: linear PCM in a WAV is lossless. AAC discards detail in exchange for a compressed stream, and was standardized as the successor to MP3.
- **Use**: WAV suits recording and editing masters. AAC is used for streaming audio and end-user delivery.

On this page, FFmpeg runs inside your browser as WebAssembly and nothing is uploaded. It ignores any video, encodes the audio with its own AAC encoder at 192 kbps and writes an ADTS stream. No sample rate, channel count, trim or volume change is set by the command. A batch of WAV files is processed one by one, and each result is a separate .aac named after its WAV. Your original WAV stays unchanged. The codec is lossy, so converting the AAC back to WAV later will not restore the audio: encode from the original WAV, and avoid editing and re-encoding the AAC again and again.

The AAC comes out as a freestanding ADTS stream. FFmpeg's ADTS muxer accepts a single AAC stream, which is why the audio is written alone, and an app that wants an MP4 wrapper should be given the M4A converter's output instead.

### Other ways to convert WAV to AAC

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i session.wav -vn -c:a aac -b:a 192k session-listen.aac` on the command line. Here -vn drops video, -c:a aac selects FFmpeg's own AAC encoder and -b:a fixes the bitrate. Add a sample rate or channel option when a delivery spec calls for one.
- **Audacity with FFmpeg:** load the WAV, open File > Export Audio and pick Custom FFmpeg Export. In the format options choose a format and an AAC codec, which depends on how FFmpeg was built. This needs Audacity's optional FFmpeg library.
- **WavePad:** open the WAV and choose File > Save As, then pick AAC. NCH lists AAC writing for Windows and Mac. Because AAC is lossy, avoid repeated editing generations of the same file.

### Problems with WAV files

- **Import fails**: some recorders put proprietary compression into the WAV, a case where Audacity suggests installing its FFmpeg library.
- **A very large recording**: the original RIFF size fields top out near 4 GB, so recordings past them may need RF64, and a program built for the old layout may not handle such a file.
- **Tags are missing or odd**: tags kept in INFO chunks and in Broadcast WAVE extensions differ, so programs treat metadata differently.
- **One WAV opens and another does not**: WAV can wrap PCM or compressed audio, so programs differ in what they accept.

guide.title: About WAV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

WAVE audio files, written .wav, use the RIFF chunk structure. Microsoft and IBM published the layout in a 1991 multimedia specification, and it describes a wrapper rather than a fixed encoding. Linear PCM is what you will usually find inside. Compressed audio is allowed too, so the extension alone cannot tell you what a given file holds. Common media types are audio/wav and audio/x-wav.

A variant called Broadcast WAVE carries extra metadata for production and preservation. The Library of Congress recommends the format for audio collections. As a source for a ringtone, a WAV is a good place to start because it usually holds uncompressed PCM, which makes files big but exact. The format record puts the original size limit at 4 GB.

### Programs that open WAV files

**Windows, Linux and Mac**

- ffplay: the player that ships with FFmpeg has a WAV demuxer, so it can play the WAV from the command line before you convert it.
- Audacity: reads the common WAV recordings, PCM variants included.

**Mobile**

- Android edition of VLC: plays media on phones and tablets, with decoding that depends on what the container holds.
- Firefox for Android: Mozilla lists WAV among the audio it plays directly.
- mpv for Android: a port the mpv project links to, which plays the WAV on a phone or tablet.

### WAV and M4R compared

- **Encoding**: WAV usually holds uncompressed linear PCM. M4R holds compressed audio, typically AAC.
- **Container**: an MPEG-4 file keeps its wrapper structure apart from whatever encoding the tracks use. MediaInfo classifies .m4r within its MPEG-4 container family, and these files can carry track metadata besides the samples.
- **Purpose**: WAV is a recording master, while NCH's WavePad manual calls M4R the iPhone's ringtone type.
- **Length**: Apple's GarageBand ringtone workflow limits the selected sound to 30 seconds, so a longer WAV has to be shortened elsewhere, because this page does not trim.
- **Support**: WavePad lists .m4r opening and saving on Windows, but not on Mac.

The conversion runs in your browser, where FFmpeg (WebAssembly) skips any video and converts the audio to AAC at 192 kbps. It writes the result with FFmpeg's iPod format, so the file is MPEG-4 audio that carries the .m4r name. The command leaves sample rate, channel count and length alone, so the ringtone runs as long as the WAV. The page does not install a ringtone either: you still have to add the M4R to the iPhone. Select a batch and every WAV is converted one at a time, each getting its own .m4r with the WAV's name. Your original WAV is not changed.

### Other ways to convert WAV to M4R

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i cue.wav -t 30 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -vn -f ipod cue-tone.m4r` on the command line. In this command -vn drops video, -c:a and -b:a choose the AAC encoder and its bitrate, and -f ipod writes the MPEG-4 container. This example cuts the audio at 30 seconds with `-t 30`. It makes the file and does not assign a ringtone.
- **WavePad on Windows:** open the WAV, then choose File > Save As and pick M4R. NCH lists M4R saving for Windows only.
- **GarageBand on iPhone:** create a recording project, then use Tracks > Loops Browser > Files > Browse items from Files to bring the WAV into Tracks and trim it. Back in My Songs, pick the project, then Share, Ringtone and Export. This builds and installs the ringtone on the phone, within the 30-second limit, and GarageBand offers to shorten a longer export. A dimmed song cannot be picked until it has been downloaded to the iPhone.

### Problems with WAV files

- **It will not import**: some recorders put proprietary compression inside a WAV. Audacity points to its FFmpeg library for those imports.
- **The file is too big for an old program**: recordings that outgrow the original RIFF size fields may be stored as RF64, which a program built for the older layout may not read.
- **A player balks at one file**: the same wrapper holds PCM or compressed audio, so one program can accept a file that another refuses.
- **Titles or tags are odd**: INFO chunks and Broadcast WAVE extensions carry different information, so metadata is handled unevenly.

faqs.question: How do I convert WMV to AVI?
faqs.answer: Select the WMV above, wait for the conversion to end and save the AVI that appears.

faqs.question: What is inside the AVI I get?
faqs.answer: MPEG-4 Part 2 video with the Xvid tag at a fixed quality value of 10 with no B-frames, and MP3 audio at 96 kbps. AVI is only the wrapper, so these two codecs are what a player has to support.

faqs.question: What is the difference between WMV and AVI?
faqs.answer: WMV is Windows Media video, usually stored in Microsoft's ASF container. AVI, a RIFF-based container from Microsoft, can carry many codecs. Changing the extension does not change what is inside, which is why the video is re-encoded.

faqs.question: Will the AVI look worse than the WMV?
faqs.answer: It can. Both formats are lossy, and the AVI is encoded from the already-compressed WMV picture. Converting does not add detail.

faqs.question: Is my video resized?
faqs.answer: Only if it is big. A frame bigger than 1920 pixels in either direction is scaled down, and a clip above 30 fps drops frames to reach it while keeping its running time. Width and height are adjusted to even numbers.

faqs.question: Does the converter deinterlace the video?
faqs.answer: When a frame is flagged interlaced, yes. The yadif filter skips everything else, so progressive video is untouched.

faqs.question: What happens to the WMV's sound?
faqs.answer: The audio is decoded, then encoded again as 96 kbps MP3 by LAME, which makes it a second lossy generation.

faqs.question: Can I rename a .wmv file to .avi?
faqs.answer: No, because the name is only a label and the bytes inside stay Windows Media. Any program that inspects the contents will reject it. Converting is what produces genuine AVI data.

faqs.question: Can I convert a batch of WMV files?
faqs.answer: Yes. Several WMVs give several AVIs, made one at a time and never joined into a single movie.

faqs.question: Is there a size limit for the WMV?
faqs.answer: The page sets none. The original AVI design had size restrictions that a later extension, OpenDML, lifted, so a very long recording may need a player that supports large AVI files.

guide.title: About WMV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMV file?

Windows Media content in the ASF container is what a WMV file holds. Microsoft designed ASF for synchronized media that can be stored on a disk or delivered over HTTP, and it carries audio and video streams. The video inside a WMV uses Windows Media Video compression, in version 7, 8 or 9, according to the Library of Congress. That entry also notes video/x-ms-wmv, a media type in common use that was never formally registered.

The ending names only the family, so two WMV files can use different compression versions. How good a WMV looks comes from the codec and settings used to make it, not from the extension.

ASF carries audio and video streams, and a file can be played from disk or fetched over HTTP. The video inside is Windows Media coded content, so the ASF wrapper and the compression are two separate things.

### Programs that open WMV files

**Windows, Linux and Mac**

- FFplay: the player that comes with FFmpeg, which decodes WMV with FFmpeg's own decoders.
- VLC media player: its feature list covers ASF and WMV input plus Windows Media Video decoders for versions 1, 2 and 9.

**Mobile**

- Android port of VLC: brings the desktop player's decoding to Android.
- iOS port of VLC: plays files on the device with VLC's own engine, not the system player.

### WMV and AVI compared

- **Extensions**: .wmv and .avi. Neither ending says which codec is inside.
- **Container**: WMV uses ASF, built for streaming and synchronized delivery. AVI, which Microsoft introduced in 1992, is built on RIFF. It interleaves timed pictures and sound, and its header records dimensions and frame rate.
- **Codecs**: a WMV carries Windows Media Video. An AVI can carry uncompressed, lossless or lossy video, identified by FOURCC codes. The AVI made here holds Xvid-tagged MPEG-4 video (Part 2).
- **Size limits**: the first AVI design restricted file size, and the later OpenDML extension relaxed that.
- **Streaming**: ASF was built for network delivery as well as disk storage, while AVI is an interleaved file of timed pictures and sound.
- **Metadata**: AVI implementations do not all handle aspect ratio and scan type the same way.

What happens to your file here: FFmpeg, running in the browser, reads the ASF container and passes any frames marked as interlaced through a deinterlacer. Video larger than 1920 pixels is reduced to fit, faster motion is limited to 30 frames per second, and widths and heights are adjusted to even values. The video is encoded with FFmpeg's MPEG-4 encoder at quality value 10 with no B-frames, and the sound goes through the LAME MP3 encoder at 96 kbps. Both codecs are lossy, so the AVI is a second generation of the picture and cannot be sharper than the WMV. The download is named after the WMV with an .avi ending, and the original is not changed. Select a batch and each WMV becomes its own AVI, converted one after another and never merged; no ZIP is produced.

### Other ways to convert WMV to AVI

- **FFmpeg:** on the command line, `ffmpeg -i legacy.wmv -c:v mpeg4 -c:a libmp3lame legacy.avi`. It reads the WMV with FFmpeg's decoder for it and writes the AVI with the two encoders named in the command. The command re-encodes both streams instead of copying them, and the -c:v and -c:a options pick the encoders. FFmpeg guesses the output container from the file extension, so the .avi name is what asks for an AVI.

### Problems with WMV files

- **Sound plays but the picture is missing**: unpacking the ASF wrapper is one job and decoding the video inside is another, and a player may manage only the first. The FFmpeg codec list itself marks its Windows Media Video 9 decoder as incomplete, so files can behave differently from program to program. Try VLC, which lists ASF and WMV input, to see whether the file opens at all.
- **Two WMV files look different**: the family covers versions 7, 8 and 9, so the picture depends on the compression and settings used to make each file. Compare the files themselves, not their extensions, when one looks worse than another.
- **A player gets the wrapper but not the video**: reading ASF does not mean every codec inside is installed.

seo.title: Convert XCF to PDF Online (Free)
seo.description: Convert a GIMP XCF to a one-page PDF in your browser. The picture is embedded losslessly as a PNG at 1 pixel per point, with no margin. Free, no sign-up.

tool.subtitle: Turn a GIMP XCF into a one-page PDF you can send to anyone, without GIMP.

faqs.question: How do I convert XCF to PDF?
faqs.answer: Select the XCF above and download the PDF produced. ImageMagick reads the file locally, so it is never sent anywhere, and several XCFs are processed one by one.

faqs.question: Do my layers become separate PDF pages?
faqs.answer: No. An XCF is read as one picture, so the PDF has one page whatever the number of layers. GIMP's own PDF export has a Layers as pages option if you want one page per layer.

faqs.question: What size is the PDF page?
faqs.answer: It matches the image, one pixel per point, so a 1200 x 800 pixel XCF yields a 1200 x 800 point page of about 16.7 x 11.1 inches. Margins and standard paper sizes do not come into it.

faqs.question: Does the PDF reduce the picture's quality?
faqs.answer: No. Pixels are embedded losslessly as a PNG, so quality settings do not come into it.

faqs.question: Can I search for words in the PDF?
faqs.answer: No. All the PDF contains is a picture, so its words cannot be searched or selected. Keep the XCF if the words still need editing.

faqs.question: Can I edit the PDF in GIMP later?
faqs.answer: Not as layers. XCF is GIMP's working format and keeps layers and transparency; the PDF holds one flat picture. Keep the XCF for future editing.

faqs.question: Why convert at all instead of sending the XCF?
faqs.answer: Most ordinary image viewers cannot read XCF. A PDF opens in any browser or PDF reader.

faqs.question: Can I combine several XCF files into one PDF?
faqs.answer: No. Each XCF becomes a separate PDF. A PDF tool can join them afterwards.

faqs.question: Is there a size limit?
faqs.answer: Roughly 537 megapixels is the ceiling, and the page then reports the file as too large.

faqs.question: Why did my XCF fail to convert?
faqs.answer: ImageMagick could not read the file. Open it in GIMP to see whether it is intact, and export a PNG from GIMP to convert that instead.

guide.title: About XCF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an XCF file?

XCF is GIMP's native working-image format. The file keeps layers and transparency, so work can be resumed later and not just viewed as one flat picture. It also keeps channels, paths and selections, and GIMP uses it to retain editing information between sessions. Undo history is left out. GIMP's Save command writes XCF, while other image formats go through Export.

GIMP does not present XCF as a format for exchanging images. It is a project file meant for your own editing, so most ordinary image viewers cannot read it. That is the usual reason to turn it into something shareable.

### Programs that open XCF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- GIMP: the native editor, and saving as XCF keeps the whole working image.
- ImageMagick: reads XCF, though an outside renderer may not reproduce every GIMP feature.

XCF is used for layered image editing and for saving work in progress, and it is lossless, so reopening the file in GIMP loses nothing.

### XCF and PDF compared

- **Purpose**: XCF is a working file for editing in GIMP. PDF is a fixed-page document made to be shared and read.
- **Layers**: XCF keeps layers and transparency. A PDF made here holds one picture on one page.
- **Page**: an XCF is a canvas of pixels. A PDF has a page size, so a viewer knows how large the page is.
- **Support**: few ordinary viewers read XCF, while PDF is readable in browsers and PDF readers.
- **Editing**: GIMP can reopen an XCF with every layer. A PDF of the picture cannot give the layers back.

Here is what the converter does. ImageMagick, compiled to WebAssembly, reads the XCF in your browser as a single picture, so layers are not turned into separate pages. The picture is then embedded in a PDF with pdf-lib. The document is one page sized to the picture, with each pixel counted as one point, so a canvas 1200 pixels wide makes a page 1200 points wide, about 16.7 inches. That leaves out margins and standard paper sizes. Inside ImageMagick the pixels are first turned into a PNG, and pdf-lib then places that PNG on the page. The picture goes in losslessly, which means the quality setting does not apply. Above about 537 megapixels the page declines the file with a note that it is too large. Several files are never combined into one PDF, and the XCF you chose is left unchanged. The download is named after the XCF with a .pdf ending.

### Other ways to convert XCF to PDF

- **GIMP:** open the XCF and choose File > Export As, or press Shift+Ctrl+E, which stores the image in a format other than XCF. Export it as PDF. The PDF options include Layers as pages, Reverse order, Root layers only, Apply layer masks, Omit hidden layers and Fill transparent areas with background color, which help for a page per layer or a solid backdrop. The dialog also offers Convert bitmaps to vector and Convert text layers to image, so check each option against what you want the PDF to hold.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick project.xcf project-review.pdf`. ImageMagick's formats page lists XCF as read-only and says PDF output needs Ghostscript installed. Compare the result with what you see in GIMP, since ImageMagick is a different renderer from GIMP.
- **GIMP and Preview on a Mac:** export the picture you want from GIMP as a PNG and open it in Preview. Then choose File > Export, open the Format pop-up menu, choose PDF and save. Preview is working from the PNG here, not the XCF.

### Problems with XCF files

- **Other software can't read it**: common image viewers do not understand XCF, so export a copy from GIMP for viewing.
- **The export is flat**: a flattened export does not keep every project property. Keep the XCF for future editing.
- **GIMP asks to save on exit**: exporting leaves the XCF project unsaved, so the prompt still appears.
- **A layered file gives one picture**: this page reads the XCF as a single image, so a layer cannot be chosen here, and layers do not become pages. GIMP's own export has Layers as pages for that.
- **It appears different elsewhere**: outside programs do not replicate all of GIMP's features. Export from GIMP itself and check the output.
